column1: # The agent execution case file (scripts/agent-exec.py; docs/agent-exec-20261012/CONTRACT.md).
# Columns, tab-separated: id declared timeout_s stdin expect text
#   id        case id (C1..C12), a trailing letter for a case's sub-calls, run in order
#   declared  session | ro | nofs: the authority the call asks for; the driver refuses a text that
#             does not ask the shell for exactly that (see CONTRACT.md "What the driver refuses")
#   timeout_s the host kills the ssh client after this many seconds
#   stdin     - (none) or @FILE relative to this directory, sent as the call's input
#   expect    space-separated: rc=N rc!=N stdout~RE stderr~RE stdout=stdin:ID refused=host-policy
#             cancelled exited=Code(N) scratch_differs=ID host_absent=PATH guest-refusal
#             concurrent=N accepted=N conn_refused=N
#   text      the exec text, exactly as an agent sends it
# Every call that runs is also checked for one exec line, one SSH SESSION CHILD line of the
# predicted route (argv: argv0=/bin/WORD spawn_right=false spares=[] control=false; shell:
# argv0=/bin/absd-sh spawn_right=true control=true), the release of that child's slot, and a
# new quiescent SERVED CAPACITY line compared with the baseline.
# C1 argv route: no spawn right, no control channel.
C1
# C2 a read of /share (read-only in every session).
C2
# C3 upload into /home/operator, then read it back under per-call read-only narrowing.
C3a
C3b
C3c
# C4 the narrowing is enforced, not advisory: the guest refuses, and the host reader finds nothing.
C4
# C5 no filesystem at all.
C5
# C6 the session's own ceiling: /bin is read-only.
C6
# C7 per-call scratch: each call sees only its own /tmp/session-<id>.
C7a
C7b
# C8 cancellation by client drop: the host kills ssh at 5 s; sshd kills the child.
C8
# C9 status transport.
C9
# C10 a machine request: refused by the driver (host policy), no connection is made.
# C11 the connection ceiling (the only overlapped case): four sessions run, the fifth is refused.
# C12 a guest-built tool run as a session command (/bin/tcc and the tcc fixture image).
# requires candidate 2
C12a
